questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How the words used on menus affect diners
How to cook classic French dishes
Why fried chicken is unhealthy
The best restaurants to eat in around Manchester
questions.why: They discuss how the language used to describe food affects our psychology.

questions.q: Why does Neil offer Beth chicken and chips twice, using different words?
options: Because he forgot what he had said the first time
Because he wants to practise his French
To show how words can make a dish sound better
To show that French food is healthier
questions.why: He says the same dish described with different words can sound more delicious.

questions.q: Why are many words for gourmet food French?
options: Because French is easier to spell
Because French food is cheaper than food from other countries
Because most chefs are French
Because France has a long tradition of high-level cooking
questions.why: Neil says France has a long tradition of high-level cooking called haute cuisine.

questions.q: According to linguist Dr Keri Matwick, why is French being used less on menus?
options: Chefs no longer learn French
It can sound pretentious
French food is less popular
It makes food more expensive
questions.why: She says there's a tendency not to use French now “because it sounds pretentious”.

questions.q: What happened when chef Caroline Martins used French cooking terms on her menu?
options: More customers came to her restaurant
Customers asked her to teach them some French cooking words
Some diners got confused, avoided dishes or even left
Critics gave her an award
questions.why: People were confused, avoided dishes, were sarcastic, and some just left.

questions.q: What does Caroline suggest her customers really wanted?
options: Cheaper prices
Simple food without fancy names
More French dishes
Smaller portions at lower prices
questions.why: She imagines them saying, “I wanna eat food, I don't wanna eat names, posh names.”

questions.q: Which languages does Caroline use on her menu now?
options: English and Brazilian Portuguese
French and English
Only Portuguese
Spanish, English and a little French
questions.why: Neil says she now uses English and her native Brazilian Portuguese.

questions.q: What has been the result of Caroline's change?
options: Customers complain about the prices
Fewer people now order the Brazilian dishes on the menu
Waiters have less to do
Customers aren't confused and chat with the waiters
questions.why: Customers don't feel confused, and their curiosity starts a conversation with the waiter.
